english: Consider the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3x+y-1}{x+2y+3}$. For $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$, let $L_\lambda$ denote the line $(3x+y-1)+\lambda(x+2y+3)=0$. There are exactly two real values $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ of $\lambda$ for which, at every point of $L_\lambda$ with $x+2y+3\neq0$, the slope of $L_\lambda$ is equal to the value of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ given by the differential equation. Then the value of $\lambda_1\lambda_2$ is ______.
hindi: अवकल समीकरण $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3x+y-1}{x+2y+3}$ पर विचार कीजिए। $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ के लिए माना कि $L_\lambda$ रेखा $(3x+y-1)+\lambda(x+2y+3)=0$ को दर्शाता है। $\lambda$ के ठीक दो वास्तविक मान $\lambda_1$ तथा $\lambda_2$ ऐसे हैं जिनके लिए $L_\lambda$ के प्रत्येक बिन्दु पर, जहाँ $x+2y+3\neq0$ है, $L_\lambda$ की प्रवणता अवकल समीकरण द्वारा दिए गए $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ के मान के बराबर है। तब $\lambda_1\lambda_2$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Every $L_\lambda$ passes through $(1,-2)$, the common point of the two lines; $X=x-1$, $Y=y+2$: $\dfrac{dY}{dX}=\dfrac{3X+Y}{X+2Y}$
$L_\lambda$ is $Y=mX$ with $m=-\dfrac{3+\lambda}{1+2\lambda}$; along it the equation gives $\dfrac{3+m}{1+2m}$
solution_full: All lines $L_\lambda$ belong to the family through the point of intersection of $3x+y-1=0$ and $x+2y+3=0$, which is $(1,-2)$.
Shift the origin there: $x=X+1$, $y=Y-2$. Then $3x+y-1=3X+Y$ and $x+2y+3=X+2Y$, so the equation becomes the homogeneous equation $\dfrac{dY}{dX}=\dfrac{3X+Y}{X+2Y}$.

The line $L_\lambda$ is $(3+\lambda)X+(1+2\lambda)Y=0$, that is, $Y=mX$ with $m=-\dfrac{3+\lambda}{1+2\lambda}$ (for $\lambda=-\frac12$ the line is $X=0$, which is not a solution since $X+2Y\neq0$ there gives a finite slope).

Along $Y=mX$ the equation gives $\dfrac{dY}{dX}=\dfrac{3X+mX}{X+2mX}=\dfrac{3+m}{1+2m}$, a constant. So $L_\lambda$ is a solution curve exactly when $m=\dfrac{3+m}{1+2m}$, that is, $m+2m^{2}=3+m$, $m^{2}=\dfrac32$, $m=\pm\sqrt{\dfrac32}$.
From $m(1+2\lambda)=-(3+\lambda)$: $\lambda(2m+1)=-(3+m)$, so $\lambda=-\dfrac{3+m}{2m+1}$, which gives one $\lambda$ for each $m$; these are $\lambda=\pm\dfrac{\sqrt6}{2}$.
originality_note: New: the straight-line solutions of a reducible-to-homogeneous equation are the members of the pencil through the centre whose slope is fixed by m = (a1 + b1 m)/(a2 + b2 m), so the parameter of the family of lines is the unknown (way 5). Closest known: solving dy/dx = (a1x + b1y + c1)/(a2x + b2y + c2) by shifting the origin. Different because: no integration is done; the link between the pencil and invariant lines is the idea, and web search found only the two ingredients separately.
blueprint_concepts: Family of lines through the intersection of two lines

concept_use.Equations reducible to homogeneous form:: Shifting the origin to (1,-2), the intersection of the two lines, makes the equation homogeneous, and a line Y = mX is a solution exactly when m = (3 + m)/(1 + 2m).
concept_use.Family of lines through the intersection: The lines L_lambda form the family through the intersection of 3x + y - 1 = 0 and x + 2y + 3 = 0; the slope of each member is -(3 + lambda)/(1 + 2 lambda).

key_step: Lines through the centre are solutions iff their slope satisfies m = (3 + m)/(1 + 2m); translate m back to lambda.
justification: Links the family of lines through an intersection point with the invariant-line condition of the shifted homogeneous equation; two ideas linked, the second unfamiliar but short. Comparable to 2021-P1-Q16 (L3) and 2023-P2-Q2 (L3).
